note: Multiple studies confirm that the recurrent heterozygous RAB3A p.Arg83Trp mutation predominantly causes adult-onset, progressive cerebellar ataxia with cerebellar cortical atrophy.

evidence.text: Affected individuals carrying the recurrent c.247C>T p.(Arg83Trp) variant presented with adult-onset, gradually progressive cerebellar symptoms, with brain MRI showing cerebellar atrophy and neuropathology demonstrating diffuse cerebellar cortical degeneration.

source.title: An R83W mutation in Rab3A causes autosomal-dominant cerebellar ataxia
source.quote: In this study, we identified the c.247C > T p.(Arg83Trp) variant in RAB3A, encoding a small GTPase involved in membrane-associated regulated exocytosis, in two families with cerebellar ataxia. Affected individuals presented with adult-onset, gradually progressive cerebellar symptoms, often accompanied by mild gait spasticity and tremors.

evidence.text: Screening of ataxia cohorts identified 18 individuals from 10 unrelated families with cerebellar ataxia, with 9 families harboring the recurrent p.Arg83Trp variant associated with pure cerebellar ataxia.

source.title: Heterozygous RAB3A variants cause cerebellar ataxia by a partial loss-of-function mechanism
source.quote: In total, we identified 18 individuals from 10 unrelated families all sharing a cerebellar ataxia phenotype. Notably, 9 of the 10 families carried a recurrent variant in RAB3A, p.Arg83Trp, including one de novo occurrence.
